findings.explanation: Before the year ends, 良いお年を wishes someone a good coming year. 'Happy New Year' is the greeting used after the new year has arrived, so the English places Koharu's earlier farewell on the wrong side of the holiday.

findings.highlight: The architect who had set up the moat around my schedule last week to be filled in
findings.evidenceJa: 先週のバイトの時に埋められていた外堀の、現場監督がそこにいた…
findings.explanation: Haruki extends 外堀を埋める, the idiom for removing someone's alternatives or laying the groundwork around them: the 'site foreman' who had filled in his outer moat last week is standing there. The English mechanically combines an architect, a moat, a schedule, and a future passive construction into a sentence with no coherent image or proposition.
findings.japanese:
先週のバイトの時に埋められていた外堀の、
現場監督がそこにいた…
findings.todokanai: The architect who had set up the moat around my schedule last week to be filled in is right here…

findings.highlight: It's just that my original intent was to give up on this little bit of rehabilitation once Sugiura caught me.
findings.evidenceJa:
ただ、杉浦に捕まった時点で、
本来はこのリハビリは諦めるべきだった。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he ought to have abandoned this rehabilitation once Koharu caught him; the English makes that his original intent.
findings.japanese:
ただ、杉浦に捕まった時点で、
本来はこのリハビリは諦めるべきだった。
findings.todokanai: It's just that my original intent was to give up on this little bit of rehabilitation once Sugiura caught me.

findings.highlight: "I take it that everything you've ordered is to your liking? In that case, please enjoy your meal."
findings.evidenceJa:
「ご注文の品、以上でよろしいでしょうか？
では、ごゆっくりどうぞ」
findings.explanation: Koharu confirms whether that is the customer's full order; the English asks whether everything ordered is to the customer's liking.
findings.japanese:
「ご注文の品、以上でよろしいでしょうか？
では、ごゆっくりどうぞ」
findings.todokanai: "I take it that everything you've ordered is to your liking? In that case, please enjoy your meal."

findings.highlight: She grew distant from others because of me… Those around her accidentally got dragged into this mess
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女のことでねじくれてさ…俺の近くにいる人たちまで無差別に巻き込んで
findings.explanation: Haruki says that he became twisted over Setsuna and indiscriminately dragged even the people around himself into it. The English makes Setsuna grow distant from others and makes people around her get dragged in accidentally, reversing the damaged person's agency, the affected social circle, and Haruki's self-accusation.
findings.japanese:
「彼女のことでねじくれてさ…
俺の近くにいる人たちまで無差別に巻き込んで」
findings.todokanai: "She grew distant from others because of me… Those around her accidentally got dragged into this mess thanks to me."

findings.explanation: Haruki calls Mihoko an important pupil he taught. The English calls her his junior, erasing the tutor–student relationship on which his responsibility, her use of 'Sensei,' and Koharu's position as the pupil's friend all depend.
findings.japanese:
「昔なじみや、大学の友達や、バイト先の同僚や、
それに…大事な教え子とか、さ」
findings.todokanai: "Close friends from the past, friends from university, fellow part-timers, and also… an important junior of mine."

findings.highlight: The best friend of an important former student of mine, who's also a colleague from work.
findings.evidenceJa:
大事な教え子の親友で、
バイト先の同僚で。
findings.explanation: Koharu is the best friend of Haruki's important pupil; the English calls the pupil a former student.
findings.japanese:
大事な教え子の親友で、
バイト先の同僚で。
findings.todokanai: The best friend of an important former student of mine, who's also a colleague from work.

findings.highlight: making me choke up a bit too
findings.evidenceJa: 杉浦がそのとき放った恨みの声は、ほんの少しだけ鼻にかかっていた。
findings.explanation: Koharu's resentful voice is slightly nasal, revealing that she herself is near tears. The English instead makes Haruki choke up, moving the emotional leak from Koharu to him and suppressing her personal investment in the exchange.
findings.japanese:
そんな大事な杉浦がそのとき放った恨みの声は、
ほんの少しだけ鼻にかかっていた。
findings.todokanai: Sugiura, who's so important to me, started voicing her resentment, making me choke up a bit too.

findings.highlight: Sugiura was completely in line with what everyone else had told her. I understand that she's only just now starting to form her own opinion
findings.evidenceJa: その時の杉浦が、一般論に混ぜて、ほんの少しだけ個別論にまで踏み込んでいることも、ちゃんとわかってた。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he understood that, back then, Koharu had mixed a small, personally specific appeal into what she framed as general principles. The English invents other people's prior opinions and says Koharu is only now beginning to form her own, reversing both the time and the nature of her earlier confession.
findings.japanese:
その時の杉浦が、一般論に混ぜて、
ほんの少しだけ個別論にまで踏み込んでいることも、
ちゃんとわかってた。
findings.todokanai: Back then, Sugiura was completely in line with what everyone else had told her. I understand that she's only just now starting to form her own opinion.

findings.evidenceJa: 相変わらず、なんて前向きな。
findings.explanation: Koharu is extraordinarily positive and forward-looking; the English calls her straightforward.
findings.japanese: 相変わらず、なんて前向きな。

findings.highlight: I've got this feeling for the first time since I was born, so I can't let it go to waste now.
findings.evidenceJa:
せっかくこの世に生を受けた今の感情を、
そのまま止めてしまうなんてことはしたくない。
findings.explanation: Haruki's newly born feeling becomes a feeling he has had for the first time since he himself was born.
findings.japanese:
せっかくこの世に生を受けた今の感情を、
そのまま止めてしまうなんてことはしたくない。
findings.todokanai: I've got this feeling for the first time since I was born, so I can't let it go to waste now.

findings.evidenceJa: そこが元から俺のバイト先だったってだけ
findings.explanation: Haruki says the place Koharu chose had already been his part-time workplace. The English says it was where he used to work, falsely implying that he no longer works there during a scene in which he has just taken a kitchen shift.
findings.japanese:
「杉浦が卒業旅行のためにバイトを始めたら、
そこが元から俺のバイト先だったってだけ。
…それ以外の理由はないよ」
findings.todokanai: "Sugiura's working part-time to fund her graduation trip, and that place just happened to be where I used to work… That's all there is to it."

findings.highlight: I was afraid of letting others get too close to me
findings.evidenceJa: 自分に向けられる好意が怖かったから。…特に、距離が近ければ近いほど
findings.explanation: Haruki was afraid of affection directed at him, especially when it came from someone already close to him. The English changes this into fear of allowing closeness itself, obscuring why Mihoko's existing trust and romantic interest—not mere intimacy—triggered his cruelty.
findings.japanese:
「あの時の俺はさ、
自分に向けられる好意が怖かったから。
…特に、距離が近ければ近いほど」
findings.todokanai: "At that time, I was afraid of letting others get too close to me. …The closer we were, the stronger my fear became."

findings.highlight: the two girls for whom I harbored equally sincere affections
findings.evidenceJa: 俺に好意を向けてくれた女の子と、俺が好意を抱いた女の子たちと
findings.explanation: The source names the girl who showed Haruki affection and the girl or girls toward whom he felt affection; it does not say those feelings were equal. The English explicitly invents 'equally sincere' love for two girls, imposing a balance on the central triangle that the Japanese carefully does not assert.
findings.japanese:
俺に好意を向けてくれた女の子と、
俺が好意を抱いた女の子たちと、
馬鹿みたいに楽しかった学園祭のステージと。
findings.todokanai: Of the girl who delivered her affections to me, of the two girls for whom I harbored equally sincere affections for, and the performance during the school festival, where the three of us together enjoyed ourselves like fools.

findings.highlight: I don't think I'd ever understand how painful that must be
findings.evidenceJa: 学校を休むほどのショックを受けた繊細な心に、どれほど強い鞭を打ったのか、俺にはわからない。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he cannot know how savagely he lashed with a whip at a delicate heart already shocked enough to miss school. The English turns this self-indicting violent agency into a passive inability to understand Mihoko's pain.
findings.japanese:
学校を休むほどのショックを受けた繊細な心に、
どれほど強い鞭を打ったのか、俺にはわからない。
findings.todokanai: Something shocking enough to make her stop going to school… I don't think I'd ever understand how painful that must be.

findings.highlight: Apologizing to her would simply be making excuses
findings.evidenceJa: 謝りたかったなんて、とんだ詭弁。
findings.explanation: Haruki recognizes that claiming he wanted to apologize was sophistry: his true purpose in arranging the meeting was to tell Mihoko why he rejected her and reject her clearly again. The English says an apology would itself be excuse-making, obscuring the distinction between his stated pretext and actual motive.
findings.japanese: 謝りたかったなんて、とんだ詭弁。
findings.todokanai: Apologizing to her would simply be making excuses.
